question.text: Narmada Infra Fund (Cat I AIF): Committed Capital INR 100 crore, fully called. Fund tenure 5 years. Terminal NAV at wind-up = INR 180 crore. Hurdle Rate 8% compounded. Carry 20%, with a 100% catch-up clause. Compute the GP carry (in INR crore).

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the workbook's Example 6.5 target-share method for 100% catch-up: the GP receives residual profits until its pre-determined share of total profits is reached. Total profit = INR 180 cr - INR 100 cr = INR 80 crore. GP carry target = 20% x INR 80 cr = INR 16 crore, matching keyed option C. The 5-year hurdle of INR 100 x (1.08)^5 = INR 146.93 cr (preferred return INR 46.93 cr) leaves residual of INR 33.07 cr, which is more than enough for the GP to fully catch up to its INR 16 cr target. The Trap: A applies 20% to a partial base (no catch-up); B uses an incorrect mix of catch-up arithmetic; D uses a fabricated hurdle figure. Note: Removed the contradictory ~INR 19.41 crore post-catch-up alternative, the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, and the LP-counter-proposal pro-tip, since those go beyond Example 6.5's target-share method on pp.126-128.
